title: Genetics & parent counselling
objectives: State recurrence risks for VACTERL-type associations versus single-gene syndromes you will be asked about.
Outline what a prenatal counselling session must cover after an anomaly scan.
List red-flag features that convert an isolated anomaly into a syndromic workup.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

Genetics hides inside other questions: DSD assessment, sacrococcygeal teratoma associations, Hirschsprung with Down syndrome, ARM with VACTERL screening. The examiner wants one thing — do you look beyond the index lesion, and can you counsel without alarming?

### The counselling frame that always works

After any antenatal or postnatal diagnosis: confirm the finding, grade severity and certainty, screen the rest of the fetus or baby (heart, spine, limbs, kidneys — the VACTERL sweep), state what is known and what is not, give management options with timelines, and document. Never quote a prognosis from a single scan image; fetal lung lesions and hydronephrosis both regress often enough that serial assessment is the plan.

### Syndromes that recur in answers

Down syndrome travels with Hirschsprung disease, duodenal atresia and AV canal defects. DSD assessment is multidisciplinary by rule — karyotype, hormones, imaging and psychology before any sex assignment or surgery. CAH (21-hydroxylase) is the commonest DSD presentation with salt wasting as the emergency. Beckwith-Wiedemann raises Wilms and hepatoblastoma surveillance. Document family history, consanguinity and previous affected pregnancies every time.

### How it is asked

Usually a sub-part: counsel parents of a fetus with CDH, CPAM or hydronephrosis; work up DSD; screen an ARM baby. Structure wins: finding → associated sweep → options → timeline → documentation.
